work: "Code of Canon Law, Book IV, Part I, Title VII: Marriage"
heading: CHAPTER VIII · THE EFFECTS OF MARRIAGE · Can. 1134 … Can. 1140

items.text: Keep the marriage bond perpetual and exclusive.
items.citation: Code of Canon Law, Book IV, Part I, Title VII: Marriage, Can. 1134
items.quote: a bond which by its nature is perpetual and exclusive

items.text: Give each other equal rights and duties in the partnership of conjugal life.
items.citation: Code of Canon Law, Book IV, Part I, Title VII: Marriage, Can. 1135
items.quote: Each spouse has an equal duty and right to those things which belong to the partnership of conjugal life.

items.text: Provide as best you can for the physical, social, cultural, moral, and religious education of your children.
items.citation: Code of Canon Law, Book IV, Part I, Title VII: Marriage, Can. 1136
items.quote: Parents have the most grave duty and the primary right to take care as best they can for the physical, social, cultural, moral, and religious education of their offspring.

work: "Code of Canon Law, Book IV, Part I, Title VII: Marriage"
heading: Art. 2 · RADICAL SANATION · Can. 1161 … Can. 1165

items.text: Persevere in conjugal life with your spouse.
items.quote: it is probable that the parties wish to persevere in conjugal life

items.text: Continue in your marital consent and do not revoke it.
items.quote: provided that the consent of each party perseveres

work: "Code of Canon Law, Book IV, Part I, Title VII: Marriage"
heading: CHAPTER VII · MARRIAGE CELEBRATED SECRETLY · Can. 1130 … Can. 1133

items.text: Do not reveal that your marriage was celebrated secretly; keep it hidden as the permission requires.
items.quote: the local ordinary, the one assisting, the witnesses, and the spouses observe secrecy about the marriage celebrated.

work: "Code of Canon Law, Book IV, Part I, Title VII: Marriage"
heading: CHAPTER X · THE CONVALIDATION OF MARRIAGE · Art. 1 · SIMPLE CONVALIDATION · Can. 1156 … Can. 1160

items.text: Before attempting convalidation, have any diriment impediment cease or be dispensed.
items.quote: it is required that the impediment ceases or is dispensed

items.text: At least the party conscious of the impediment must renew consent.
items.quote: at least the party conscious of the impediment renews consent

items.text: Renew consent for the validity of convalidation even if both gave consent at the beginning and did not revoke it.
items.quote: Ecclesiastical law requires this renewal for the validity of the convalidation even if each party gave consent at the beginning and did not revoke it afterwards.

items.text: Make the renewal of consent a new act of the will concerning a marriage you know or think was null from the beginning.
items.quote: The renewal of consent must be a new act of the will concerning a marriage which the renewing party knows or thinks was null from the beginning.

items.text: If the impediment is public, both must renew consent in canonical form.
items.quote: If the impediment is public, both parties must renew the consent in canonical form

items.text: If the impediment cannot be proven, let the conscious party renew consent privately and secretly while the other perseveres; if both know it, both must renew.
items.quote: If the impediment cannot be proven, it is sufficient that the party conscious of the impediment renews the consent privately and in secret, provided that the other perseveres in the consent offered

items.text: If the marriage was invalid due to a defect of consent, the party who did not consent must now consent, provided the other's consent perseveres; if the defect is provable, give this consent in canonical form; if not, give it privately and secretly.
items.quote: the party who did not consent now consents, provided that the consent given by the other party perseveres

items.text: If the marriage is null because of defect of form, contract it anew in canonical form to become valid.
items.quote: A marriage which is null because of defect of form must be contracted anew in canonical form in order to become valid

work: "Code of Canon Law, Book IV, Part I, Title VII: Marriage"
heading: CHAPTER VI · MIXED MARRIAGES · Can. 1124 … Can. 1129

items.text: Do all in your power so that your children are baptized and brought up in the Catholic Church.
items.quote: do all in his or her power so that all offspring are baptized and brought up in the Catholic Church

items.text: Inform your spouse of the promise and obligation you have made to raise your children Catholic.
items.quote: the other party is to be informed at an appropriate time about the promises which the Catholic party is to make

items.text: Do not exclude the purposes and essential properties of marriage.
items.quote: both parties are to be instructed about the purposes and essential properties of marriage which neither of the contracting parties is to exclude

items.text: Foster the unity of your conjugal and family life.
items.quote: help spouses foster the unity of conjugal and family life

work: "Code of Canon Law, Book IV, Part I, Title VII: Marriage"
heading: CHAPTER I · PASTORAL CARE AND THOSE THINGS WHICH MUST PRECEDE THE CELEBRATION OF MARRIAGE · Can. 1063 … Can. 1072

items.text: Preserve and protect the conjugal covenant faithfully, and live holier and fuller lives together in your family.
items.quote: help offered to those who are married, so that faithfully preserving and protecting the conjugal covenant

items.text: Fulfill the natural obligations you owe to your children from a previous union before you enter a new marriage.
items.quote: bound by natural obligations toward another party or children arising from a previous union

items.text: Fulfill the natural obligations you owe to the other party of your previous union before you enter a new marriage.
items.quote: bound by natural obligations toward another party or children arising from a previous union

items.text: Do not enter marriage while your parents are unaware or reasonably opposed.
items.quote: a marriage of a minor child when the parents are unaware or reasonably opposed

work: "Code of Canon Law, Book IV, Part I, Title VII: Marriage"
heading: TITLE VII · MARRIAGE (Cann. 1055 - 1165) · Can. 1055 … Can. 1062

items.text: Establish between yourselves a partnership of the whole of life, ordered to the good of the spouses and the procreation and education of offspring.
items.citation: Code of Canon Law, Title VII Marriage, Can. 1055 §1
items.quote: a partnership of the whole of life and which is ordered by its nature to the good of the spouses and the procreation and education of offspring

items.text: Keep your marriage one and indissoluble.
items.citation: Code of Canon Law, Title VII Marriage, Can. 1056
items.quote: The essential properties of marriage are unity and indissolubility

items.text: Give and accept each other through an irrevocable covenant in order to establish marriage.
items.citation: Code of Canon Law, Title VII Marriage, Can. 1057 §2
items.quote: a man and a woman mutually give and accept each other through an irrevocable covenant in order to establish marriage

items.text: Educate your children, for marriage is ordered to the procreation and education of offspring.
items.citation: Code of Canon Law, Title VII Marriage, Can. 1055 §1
items.quote: the procreation and education of offspring

work: "Code of Canon Law, Book IV, Part I, Title VII: Marriage"
heading: CHAPTER IV · MATRIMONIAL CONSENT · Can. 1095 … Can. 1107

items.text: Hand over and accept the essential rights and duties of marriage mutually.
items.citation: Code of Canon Law, Matrimonial Consent Can. 1095
items.quote: essential matrimonial rights and duties mutually to be handed over and accepted

items.text: Enter marriage knowing it is a permanent partnership between a man and a woman ordered to the procreation of offspring by sexual cooperation.
items.citation: Code of Canon Law, Matrimonial Consent Can. 1096
items.quote: marriage is a permanent partnership between a man and a woman ordered to the procreation of offspring by means of some sexual cooperation.

items.text: Do not obtain consent by malicious deceit about a quality that by its very nature can gravely disturb conjugal life.
items.citation: Code of Canon Law, Matrimonial Consent Can. 1098
items.quote: deceived by malice, perpetrated to obtain consent, concerning some quality of the other partner which by its very nature can gravely disturb the partnership of conjugal life.

items.text: Let internal consent conform to the words and signs used in marrying, and do not positively exclude marriage itself or an essential element or property.
items.citation: Code of Canon Law, Matrimonial Consent Can. 1101
items.quote: exclude marriage itself, some essential element of marriage, or some essential property of marriage

items.text: Do not make marriage subject to a condition about the future.
items.citation: Code of Canon Law, Matrimonial Consent Can. 1102
items.quote: A marriage subject to a condition about the future cannot be contracted validly.

items.text: Be present together and express matrimonial consent in words or, if unable to speak, through equivalent signs.
items.citation: Code of Canon Law, Matrimonial Consent Can. 1104
items.quote: Those being married are to express matrimonial consent in words or, if they cannot speak, through equivalent signs.

work: "Code of Canon Law, Book IV, Part I, Title VII: Marriage"
heading: Art. 2 · SEPARATION WITH THE BOND REMAINING · Can. 1151 … Can. 1155

items.text: Preserve conjugal living unless a legitimate cause excuses you.
items.citation: Code of Canon Law, Art. 2, Can. 1151
items.quote: Spouses have the duty and right to preserve conjugal living unless a legitimate cause excuses them.

items.text: Do not cause grave mental or physical danger to your spouse or otherwise render common life too difficult.
items.citation: Code of Canon Law, Art. 2, Can. 1153 §1
items.quote: If either of the spouses causes grave mental or physical danger to the other spouse or to the offspring or otherwise renders common life too difficult

items.text: When the cause for separation ceases, restore conjugal living unless the ecclesiastical authority has established otherwise.
items.citation: Code of Canon Law, Art. 2, Can. 1153 §2
items.quote: when the cause for the separation ceases, conjugal living must be restored unless ecclesiastical authority has established otherwise

items.text: After separation, always provide suitably for the support and education of the children.
items.citation: Code of Canon Law, Art. 2, Can. 1154
items.quote: the adequate support and education of the children must always be suitably provided

work: "Code of Canon Law, Book IV, Part I, Title VII: Marriage"
heading: CHAPTER IX · THE SEPARATION OF SPOUSES · Art. 1 · DISSOLUTION OF THE BOND · Can. 1141 … Can. 1150

items.text: Regard a ratified and consummated marriage as binding until death; do not attempt to dissolve it by any human power or cause.
items.quote: A marriage that is ratum et consummatum can be dissolved by no human power and by no cause, except death.
items.conflict: Scripture permits divorce for sexual immorality and desertion; absolute indissolubility extends beyond biblical grounds.

items.text: Do not remarry under the Pauline privilege unless your unbaptized spouse departs; if he or she is willing to live peacefully with you, remain married.
items.quote: provided that the non-baptized party departs

items.text: After baptism, do not give your unbaptized spouse a just cause for departing; live peacefully without affront to God.
items.quote: unless the baptized party, after baptism was received, has given the other a just cause for departing

items.text: Before contracting a new marriage under the Pauline privilege, ask your non-baptized spouse whether he or she will receive baptism or at least live with you peacefully without affront to God.
items.quote: the non-baptized party must always be interrogated whether: 1/ he or she also wishes to receive baptism; 2/ he or she at least wishes to cohabit peacefully

items.text: If a baptized husband has several non-baptized wives, retain only one after dismissing the others, and provide sufficiently for the dismissed wives.
items.quote: the needs of the first wife and the others dismissed are sufficiently provided for according to the norms of justice, Christian charity, and natural equity
items.conflict: Polygamy contradicts the one-flesh pattern of Genesis 2:24 and Matthew 19:5-6; provision remains required.

items.text: If a baptized wife has several non-baptized husbands, retain only one after dismissing the others, and provide sufficiently for the dismissed husbands.
items.quote: The same is valid for a non-baptized woman who has several non-baptized husbands at the same time.
items.conflict: Polyandry contradicts the one-flesh pattern of Genesis 2:24 and Matthew 19:5-6; provision remains required.

work: "Code of Canon Law, Book IV, Part I, Title VII: Marriage"
heading: CHAPTER III · SPECIFIC DIRIMENT IMPEDIMENTS · Can. 1083 … Can. 1094

items.text: While the bond of your marriage stands, do not attempt marriage with another, even if your marriage was not consummated.
items.quote: A person bound by the bond of a prior marriage, even if it was not consummated, invalidly attempts marriage.

items.text: Never bring about your spouse's death, alone or with another, in order to marry someone else.
items.quote: Anyone who with a view to entering marriage with a certain person has brought about the death of that person’s spouse or of one’s own spouse invalidly attempts this marriage.

items.text: Do not marry a close blood relative within the direct line or within the fourth degree of the collateral line.
items.quote: In the direct line of consanguinity marriage is invalid between all ancestors and descendants… In the collateral line marriage is invalid up to and including the fourth degree.

items.text: Do not marry your spouse's parent, even after your spouse's death.
items.quote: Affinity in the direct line in any degree invalidates a marriage.

items.text: Do not marry your spouse's child, even after your spouse's death.
items.quote: Affinity in the direct line in any degree invalidates a marriage.

items.text: After notorious or public concubinage or an invalid marriage with common life, do not marry your partner's parent or child.
items.quote: The impediment of public propriety arises from an invalid marriage after the establishment of common life or from notorious or public concubinage.
items.conflict: No biblical warrant for treating concubinage or an invalid marriage as creating a kinship impediment; binds where Scripture has not bound.

items.text: Do not marry your adoptive parent or adoptive child.
items.quote: Those who are related in the direct line or in the second degree of the collateral line by a legal relationship arising from adoption cannot contract marriage together validly.

items.text: Do not marry an adoptive sibling within the second degree of the collateral line.
items.quote: Those who are related in the direct line or in the second degree of the collateral line by a legal relationship arising from adoption cannot contract marriage together validly.
